subject: Stepwise Dedicated Delivery: proposed ramp calendar & term adjustments
messages:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@aurorarobotics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stepwise Dedicated Delivery: proposed ramp calendar & term adjustments

Hi Megan —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Per our conversation I've sketched a stepwise delivery calendar that balances Aurora's launch milestones with predictable unit economics on our side. Key points in this proposal: 

- 36-month committed term with annual prepay options
- Year 1: 20% of committed GPU fleet + 30% of target TPM capacity (soft start)
- Year 2: 60% of GPUs + 70% TPM (scale phase)
- Year 3: 100% GPUs + 100% TPM capacity (steady state)
- Proposed term discount: 17% off list for full 3-year prepay; annual prepay options at 12% for year-by-year commits

I'm attaching a clean term sheet and a simple calendar (capacity-ramp-calendar.xlsx) for your internal stakeholders. If you'd like we can also run a 30-day pilot on a small shard to validate latency and cost assumptions before the Year 1 ramp milestone.

Next steps I suggest: 
1) Review term sheet with procurement and legal (I can loop in our counsel if needed)
2) Confirm preferred billing cadence (annual prepay vs single 3-yr prepay)
3) Lock target milestones for Q3 launch so we can reserve the GPU pool

Would you be available early next week for a short call with your infra lead to lock the ramp windows?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: aurora-term-sheet-v2.pdf (pdf), capacity-ramp-calendar.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Megan Liu <megan.liu@aurorarobotics.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stepwise Dedicated Delivery: proposed ramp calendar & term adjustments

Lauren —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick reactions from me and procurement: 

- The staged ramp looks sensible; our product timeline needs the Year 2 scale to be in production by Sep 2028 ideally.
- Procurement is pushing back on the 17% all-up prepay discount — they asked whether we can get closer to 20% for a 3-yr prepay, or otherwise a larger discount front-loaded in Year 1 while Year 3 stays at a smaller effective discount.
- We also have questions on how unused TPM capacity is handled during Year 1 (credit back or rolled forward?).

I cc'd our procurement alias so they can weigh in. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports a credit-roll mechanism for unused TPM in Year 1 and whether you can provide a slightly higher up-front discount to make the capex model easier for our CFO.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call next Tue morning PT.

—Megan
Megan Liu
VP Product, Aurora Robotics

Forwarding procurement's note to Ben and Vivek to align on feasible commercial levers. Inline below is the ask: Aurora requests ~20% up-front discount on a 3-yr prepay, or alternatively a front-loaded discount profile; they also want clarity on unused TPM handling for Year 1.

Ben / Vivek — can you review and advise on (a) whether we can move to 19.5% for a 3-yr prepay as a one-time concession tied to a signed MSA by May 15, and (b) whether we can implement a credit-roll mechanism capped at 20% of Year-1 TPM if they stay within overall committed tokens for the term?

I'm available to talk 10:00–11:00 PT today if helpful.

Thanks,
Lauren

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Stepwise Dedicated Delivery: proposed ramp calendar & term adjustments

Lauren / Vivek —

High level thoughts: we can accommodate a commercial structure that approximates what Aurora is asking but need to bind it to operational constraints to protect unit economics. Options we can offer: 

1) 3yr prepaid @ 19% if signed by May 15 and with a committed GPU pool minimum (no more than 8 week provisioning lag). TPM credit-roll: allow unused Year-1 TPM to roll into Year-2 up to 25% of Year-1 commit, but only as non-transferable credits against themselves (no cash refunds).

2) Front-loaded discount: Year1 22% effective, Year2 16%, Year3 12% (blend ~ 16.7%) if they prefer better up-front economics; requires a 10% non-refundable deposit to secure early GPUs in Q3.

3) Annual prepay path: 12% per year with right-to-increase capacity at pre-agreed list price; more flexible but worse blended discount.

Operational caveats: a) we will prioritize customers with confirmed prepay for initial provisioning windows; b) credits require usage metering tags so we can reconcile TPM usage; c) reserved GPUs must be pinned to Aurora's dedicated pool and cannot be subleased.

Recommend we offer option 1 as the baseline, present option 2 as a 'cash-friendlier' alternative, and keep option 3 as a fallback. Happy to join the Tue morning call with Aurora.

Ben
VP Sales Ops

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Stepwise Dedicated Delivery: proposed ramp calendar & term adjustments

Echo Ben's take. A couple of additional implementation notes from infra: 

- TPM credits: we'll implement credit buckets at the tenant level and allow rollover once into Year-2; we'll track with a usage tag and provide monthly reconciliation reports.
- Provisioning windows: if Aurora signs the MSA and prepays for Year 1 by May 15, we can guarantee allocation of the Q3 tranche; otherwise we'll move them to the next available window (which could slip up to 8–12 weeks).
- We'll need a short pilot plan (30-day shard) that includes target latency SLOs and a small committed TPM floor so we can validate KV cache behavior before Year 2 scale.

From an accounting perspective, front-loaded discounts create more complex revenue recognition but are doable for a negotiated enterprise deal — finance will want the term sheet to include the deposit and cancellation clauses clearly.

Vivek
Head of Product Partnerships

Hi Megan / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on internal alignment here are three clear options you can present to your CFO and procurement: 

Option A (Recommended): 3yr prepaid, 19% total discount, TPM credit-roll: unused Year-1 TPM rolls into Year-2 up to 25% of Year-1 commit. MSA signature + full prepay by May 15 to secure Q3 provisioning.

Option B (Front-loaded): 3yr prepaid with front-loaded pricing — Year1 22% / Year2 16% / Year3 12% (blended ~16.7%). Requires 10% non-refundable deposit to reserve Q3 GPUs.

Option C (Annual): Year-by-year prepay at 12% per year, more flexible but lower blended discount and no guaranteed provisioning priority.

Attachments: updated term sheet (aurora-term-sheet-v2.pdf) and the ramp calendar. I've also created a DocuSign envelope to speed sign-off: https://www.docusign.com/sign/aurora-1462.

If this looks good I propose a 30-minute call Tue 08:30 PT to run through final questions and agree a sign date. Please let me know what time works.
